Commentary.Commentary: Right then, the match is nicely poised at the halfway mark. One feels that Zimbabwe have their noses slightly ahead at this stage. Namibia's batting unit will have to step up and take their side over the line here. Can they rise to the occasion? We will find out after we return for the chase.

As far as Namibia are concerned, their bowlers were unable to set the tone early as they failed to get breakthroughs, nor did they manage to keep the runs under check in the powerplay. After the field restrictions were lifted, Namibia's skipper, Gerhard Erasmus, took matters into his own hands and wrestled the initiative back with twin blows. The rest of the bowling unit chipped in as well and did not allow Zimbabwe to form any partnerships. However, Gerhard Erasmus will be disappointed with how things panned out in the final over, as they were unable to finish strongly with the ball. That said, Erasmus was the pick of the bowlers for Namibia with figures of 2 for 21 from his four overs. Handre Klazinga was a bit expensive but accounted for two wickets as well.

Zimbabwe finish on a high with 15 runs off the final over! They would have wanted much more than what they eventually got but thanks to skipper Craig Ervine's 54 runs off 43 balls, they have a competitive total on the board. After opting to bat first, Zimbabwe were off to a flier, courtesy of their openers. Innocent Kaia got himself going with a couple of boundaries, but a mix-up led to his downfall. His opening partner, Tinashe Kamunhukamwe, took the mantle and ensured that Zimbabwe were off to a solid start. However, he was not able to carry on after the powerplay, and the early departure of Sikandar Raza put Zimbabwe in a spot of bother. Despite the consistent fall of wickets at the other end, Craig Ervin carried on and made sure that Zimbabwe did not lose their way. He batted through for his side and found support towards the end from Faraz Akram which helped Zimbabwe cross the 150-run mark.

TOSS - Zimbabwe have won the coin toss and they have elected to BAT first.

Before a ball was bowled in the series, Zimbabwe were the favourites to clinch the series, and they now find themselves a win away from doing that. After failing to put a good score on the board in the 1st T20I, the batting unit needed to step up, and they have done just that. With the ball, they have blown hot and cold, and it is an aspect that Craig Ervine's men would want to improve on. Will Zimbabwe manage to take an unassailable lead in the series? Or will Namibia bring the series back on level terms? Let's find out. Toss and team news coming up shortly.

Having drawn first blood in the series, Namibia were high on confidence but have since been given a reality check by Zimbabwe. It is last chance saloon for Gerhard Erasmus's men to keep the series alive. If it were their bowlers who were unable to defend a big total in the 2nd T20I, it was the batting that let them down in the 3rd T20I. If Namibia are to force a series decider, they would have to click collectively as a unit.

Hello and a warm welcome, ladies and gentlemen, to our coverage of the 4th T20I of the five-match series between Namibia and Zimbabwe at the United Cricket Club Ground in Windhoek. After suffering a defeat in the series opener, Zimbabwe have bounced back by registering two convincing wins and currently hold a 2-1 lead in the series.
